question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

An arm and a leg
solution:
The correct answer is "**Very expensive**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The idiom "an arm and a leg" means something is very expensive or costs a lot of money**.

 
 
• This idiom is often used to express that something is not worth the high cost.
 
• Example: "I really want that new car, but it costs an arm and a leg."
 
 
 
• "Expensive" means something that costs a lot of money.(महँगा)
 
• Thus, option 2 best describes the given idiom.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.
